title: Finite-Design Inference for Adaptively Clipped AIPW with Dense Gaussian Nuisances
banked_reason: The clipping oracle minimizes only the realized conditional outcome-noise component, not total MSE or a population variance, and the note proves no deterministic variance curve, clip-selection consistency, or strict improvement over the unclipped estimator.
gap_reasons: The clipping oracle minimizes only the realized conditional outcome-noise component, not total MSE or a population variance, and the note proves no deterministic variance curve, clip-selection consistency, or strict improvement over the unclipped estimator.
The Jiang endpoint proposition is an exact normalization back to the published estimator rather than a new endpoint extension.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery attempted a deterministic clipped covariance kernel and strict population variance gain, but two solver rounds left the cyclic leave-one-out step open. The final sound incremental result proves an exact conditional Gaussian decomposition, total pilot calibration, a realized conditional-noise clipping oracle, and conservative ATE intervals. A future field-tier attempt must establish a deterministic variance curve, selected-clip inference, and a strict gain over no clipping.
tldr: Finite-design inference for adaptively clipped AIPW with dense Gaussian nuisances. The general results require only a finite positive ridge penalty at each index, not convergence or a compact tuning range. A totalized independent-pilot construction calibrates the realized conditional-noise curve, and a two-dimensional Gaussian confidence-ball projection gives honest coverage for every design-and-pilot-measurable clip of the unchanged full ATE; the selected estimator remains root-\(N\) tight. Invariant convergence and a fixed positive ridge penalty are imposed only for the no-intercept, unclipped Jiang endpoint comparison.
gap: Jiang et al.'s published Theorem 3.4 covers the no-intercept unclipped endpoint under explicit signal-norm, correlation, coordinate Wasserstein--2, fixed-penalty, and OLS-existence hypotheses, and leaves winsorized sampling theory and feasible variance estimation open. Ma and Wang study shrinking hard trimming for IPW under regular variation with non-root-sample-size normalization and bias correction; Heiler and Kazak study untrimmed IPW and doubly robust full-ATE inference with alpha-stable limits and an adaptive subsampling law. None treats a fixed clip with persistent proportional-dimensional nuisance covariance.
fill: The project proves the precise Jiang endpoint reduction on the fully shared signal-regular submodel, derives the fitted-intercept mixed-clip kernel and a total observed covariance surface along every admissible sequence, validates tie-robust clip selection and studentization, and certifies an open region where positive clipping strictly improves on the unclipped endpoint.
